source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.2.6 heading and opening sentences, from `Let X_1, ..., X_N be independent random variables` through `for every i`
source_evidence.observation: The theorem concerns a finite family of independent random variables and assumes that each X_i lies in its own closed interval [m_i, M_i].

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.2.6 sentence `Then, for any t > 0, we have` and the following display
source_evidence.observation: For every positive threshold t, the probability that the centered unweighted sum is at least t is bounded by exp(-2 t^2 / sum_{i=1}^N (M_i-m_i)^2).

source_evidence.anchor: Paragraph immediately before Theorem 2.2.6, beginning `Our proof of Hoeffding's inequality`
source_evidence.observation: The source presents Theorem 2.2.6 as an extension of the moment-generating-function proof of Hoeffding's inequality from symmetric Bernoulli variables to general bounded random variables.
The follow-up exercise asks for a proof of Theorem 2.2.6, possibly with an absolute constant in place of 2, confirming that the displayed theorem's numerator uses the specific constant 2.

binders: N: the finite index endpoint appearing in X_1, ..., X_N and in sums from i=1 to N; its type and positivity are implicit rather than separately quantified. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; Theorem 2.2.6 opening and displayed inequality]

X_1, ..., X_N: random variables; a common underlying probability space is implicit in the joint independence assertion, probability, and sum. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; Theorem 2.2.6 opening and displayed inequality]

m_i and M_i for i=1, ..., N: endpoints of the closed interval [m_i, M_i] bounding X_i, implicitly real because the variables are summed and centered in the displayed real-valued tail inequality. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; assumption `X_i in [m_i, M_i]` and displayed inequality]
t: a threshold quantified by `for any t > 0`. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; sentence immediately preceding the display]
hypotheses: The family X_1, ..., X_N is independent. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; first sentence of Theorem 2.2.6]
For every index i, X_i belongs to the closed interval [m_i, M_i]. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; second sentence of Theorem 2.2.6]
The threshold satisfies t > 0. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; sentence immediately preceding the displayed bound]
conclusions: P{sum_{i=1}^N (X_i - E X_i) >= t} <= exp(-2 t^2 / sum_{i=1}^N (M_i - m_i)^2). [PDF page 6; printed page 17; sole display in Theorem 2.2.6]
definitions_and_conventions: E X_i denotes the expectation of X_i, and each summand is centered separately as X_i - E X_i. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; left-hand event in the theorem display]
P{...} denotes the probability of the event inside braces. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; left-hand side of the theorem display]

[m_i, M_i] is a closed bounding interval, and its length M_i-m_i enters the bound only through the square (M_i-m_i)^2. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; boundedness assumption and denominator in the theorem display]
The sum is the unweighted finite sum over every i from 1 through N. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; both sums in the theorem display]

The right-hand side is the exponential of the negative ratio whose numerator is exactly 2t^2 and whose denominator is exactly sum_{i=1}^N (M_i-m_i)^2. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; right-hand side of the theorem display]
implicit_context: The theorem is introduced as the general-bounded-random-variable extension of Hoeffding's inequality obtained by the flexible moment-generating-function method. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; paragraph immediately before Theorem 2.2.6]

Real-valuedness and existence of the expectations are implicit in the interval-membership and centered-sum notation; boundedness supplies integrability under the usual probability-theory convention. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; assumption `X_i in [m_i, M_i]` and displayed use of E X_i]

No identical-distribution, common-bound, symmetry, Bernoulli, or mean-zero assumption is stated; the theorem instead allows an index-dependent interval [m_i, M_i] and centers each variable by its own expectation. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; complete statement of Theorem 2.2.6]

details: The event is the upper tail `centered sum >= t`; the theorem does not state an absolute-value or lower-tail event. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; left-hand event in the theorem display]
There is no multiplicative factor 2 outside the exponential in this one-sided bound. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; right-hand side of the theorem display]

The random variables X_i are the summands, E X_i are deterministic centering terms, and m_i, M_i are deterministic interval endpoints controlling the concentration scale. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; hypotheses and displayed inequality]
The theorem bounds the raw sum of centered variables and does not divide by N or otherwise normalize the sum. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; left-hand event in the theorem display]
The exponent is negative and quadratic in t, with exact numerator 2t^2. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; exponent in the displayed bound]
The denominator is the sum of the squared individual interval widths, not the square of a sum and not a variance. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; denominator in the displayed bound]
The independence and interval assumptions apply to all indices i=1, ..., N, and the bound is asserted for every real threshold t>0. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; complete theorem statement]

Beyond independence and boundedness in possibly different intervals, the theorem imposes no distributional form on the X_i. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; lead-in describing `general bounded random variables` and complete theorem statement]

undebatable_constraints: The result must concern the entire finite family X_1, ..., X_N and must require their independence. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; first sentence of Theorem 2.2.6]
Each X_i must be bounded in its own closed interval [m_i, M_i] for every i. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; second sentence of Theorem 2.2.6]
The threshold quantifier is `for any t > 0`; positivity is strict. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; sentence preceding the display]
The event must be the one-sided upper event sum_{i=1}^N (X_i-E X_i) >= t, with each variable centered by its own expectation. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; left-hand event in the theorem display]

The right-hand side must be exp(-2t^2 / sum_{i=1}^N (M_i-m_i)^2), including the negative sign, the exact constant 2, and the sum of squared widths. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; right-hand side of the theorem display]
The displayed one-sided conclusion has no leading factor 2 and contains no weights or normalization by N. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; complete displayed inequality]

ambiguities.issue: The statement writes `X_i in [m_i, M_i]` without saying whether interval membership is pointwise or almost sure.
ambiguities.evidence: The boundedness assumption contains no qualifier such as `almost surely`. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; second sentence of Theorem 2.2.6]
ambiguities.impact: Under the usual probability-theory reading this is an almost-sure bound, but a formal pointwise bound is stronger as a property of chosen representatives; the source alone does not explicitly settle that representational distinction.

ambiguities.issue: The displayed real-valued formula does not separately handle a zero denominator when every interval width M_i-m_i is zero.
ambiguities.evidence: The source assumes only `X_i in [m_i, M_i]` and displays division by sum_{i=1}^N (M_i-m_i)^2; it does not state that this sum is positive or give a degenerate-case convention. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; complete Theorem 2.2.6 statement]
ambiguities.impact: If at least one width is positive, the displayed expression has its ordinary real meaning. If all widths vanish, the centered sum is degenerate under the intended boundedness reading, but interpreting the printed exponential bound requires an unstated extended-real convention or a separate trivial case.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not explicitly declare the type of N or state N >= 1.
ambiguities.evidence: N appears only through the notation X_1, ..., X_N and sums from i=1 to N. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; opening and displayed inequality of Theorem 2.2.6]
ambiguities.impact: The ordinary finite-family notation strongly suggests a positive integer N, but the source does not expressly specify behavior for an empty family.

contract_plain_english: For a finite family of independent bounded random variables X_1, ..., X_N, where X_i lies in [m_i, M_i], every positive threshold t satisfies the one-sided Hoeffding bound P{sum_{i=1}^N (X_i-E X_i) >= t} <= exp(-2t^2 / sum_{i=1}^N (M_i-m_i)^2). The variables need not be identically distributed, symmetric, or mean zero, because each is centered by its own expectation and may have its own bounding interval. [PDF page 6; printed page 17; full statement of Theorem 2.2.6 and its immediate lead-in]
